Samir — thanks and great to hear the demo resonated. Quick sketch below (high level) and I attached a numeric example for the pilot and a cap scenario for production. Ben and Irene added notes where helpful.

Option A (Pilot-first, amortized platform fee)
- Pilot (3 months): no platform fee, metered usage + reserved node pricing; 8 GPU-eq baseline; expected token rate billing.
- Conversion: 12-month commitment. Platform fee amortized over first 3 invoices (we can offer a 30% cap on first-quarter platform fee exposure).

Option B (Upfront platform fee + lower support tier)
- Small upfront platform activation (one-time) + lower ongoing platform fee rate; choose Bronze support (business hours, 24h on-call for severity 1 during SLA windows) to reduce OPEX.

Tradeoffs: lower support tier reduces SRE involvement for upgrades and on-call; amortization defers cash but increases total billed amount slightly. Attached sheet models both with raw numbers and example invoice timings.

Naoko — thanks, quick clarifications on support and credits:

Support tiers (short):
- Bronze (pilot): business-hours only, 8x5, automated patch window; ticket SLA 24h for non-sev1.
- Silver-lite (proposed): 24/7 critical monitoring + monthly ops review, on-call for sev1 within 2 hours; excludes continuous SRE runbook ops or dedicated rotation. 40% reduction vs Silver is doable for the pilot-to-prod transition if we accept narrower runbook coverage.

Implementation credits: yes, credits can be applied to SOW milestone invoices (we typically apply credits against the implementation milestone invoice and clearly call them out in the SOW appendix). Credits cannot be used against usage token billing once the system is live.

Platform-fee cap: we can accept a $40k Y1 cap as long as there is an agreed uplift threshold (e.g., sustained average utilization >150% of baseline for 60 days triggers an overage schedule). I'll flag product to bake trigger language into the SOW.
